SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.761/2017 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT OF RS.15,00,000/- AND ALSO ENHANCE THE INTEREST PAYABLE BY THE RESPONDENTS ON THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT AND FURTHER BE PLEASED TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL AND ETC.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 15.08.2016.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 15.08.2016 at about 4:30 a.m., petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-03-AP-3626 (for short 'motorcycle') on NH-218.

Near Firozabad about one and half kilometer distance to Shahabad cross, a tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-32-T-1722 ('offending vehicle' for short), being driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came and dashed against motorcycle of the petitioner.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Respondents have filed separate written statement disputing that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
Respondent No.2 further pleaded that since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence it is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the appeal.
5. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
6. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 12.

sentences.text: On behalf of respondents, RW1 and 2 are examined and Exs.R1 to 3 are marked.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,24,400/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:
Sl. Nature of the heads Compensation No.
1. Pain & sufferings Rs.30,000/-
2. Attendant charges, food and Rs.7,500/-
conveyance charges 3. Loss of future income Rs.2,28,500/-

4. Medical expenses Rs.3,24,400/-
5. Loss of income during treatment Rs.14,000/-
6. Loss of amenities and nutrition food Rs.20,000/-
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
10. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Heard arguments and perused the records.
13.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.

sentences.text: Based on the wound certificate, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 32 years and appropriate multiplier as 16.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
Since the accident is of the year 2016, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.8,750/- p.m.
Based on the evidence of PW.2 and the material placed on record, the Tribunal has rightly taken the disability at 17%.

With these components, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.8750/- x 12 x 16 x 17% =
Rs.2,85,600/- as against Rs.2,28,500/- granted by the Tribunal.
15.
Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.3,24,400/- under the head medical expenses is correct.

At the rate of Rs.8,750/- for a period of three months, petitioner is entitled compensation in a sum of Rs.26,250/- under the head loss of income during laid up period as against Rs.14,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

16. Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the period of treatment and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain & suffering, Rs.7,500/- under the head attendant charges, food nutrition and miscellaneous and Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of amenities is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and 40,000/- respectively.
17. The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head loss of future medical expenses.
Looking to the nature of injuries suffered, it would be just and reasonable to grant compensation in a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

18. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.7,51,250/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rss.6,24,400/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

income

4. Medical expenses Rs.3,24,400/- Rs.3,24,400/-
5. Loss of income Rs.14,000/- Rs.26,250/-
 during treatment 6. Loss of amenities Rs.20,000/- Rs.40,000/-
 and nutrition food 7.

Future medical ---- Rs.20,000/-
 expenses

Total Rs.6,24,400/- Rs.7,51,250/-
19. Of course petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of 6% p.a., except on Rs.20,000/- granted under the head future medical expenses.

To this extent, the appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.7,51,250/- as against Rs.6,24,400/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a., except on Rs.25,000/- granted under the head future medical expenses.

(iii) Respondent No.2/insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
